S2 makes ownership between implementer groups enforceable and adds a recorded closure rule.

Threat model (18.0). S2 defends against accidental or LLM-plausible cross-group writes, mainly by project code an agent runs, through relative or absolute paths, symlinks or git. Hostile git tampering is left to content-hash checks; OS isolation is a named limit. The copy prevents writes through relative paths. The real-tree hash detects other writes and fails the run, but does not undo them.

Ownership map (18.1, 18.2). The effective map is the hash-sealed breakdown.json groups, with reviewer amendments applied in log order. Each amendment's "from" equals the globs in force, and every map passes the GF-WBS-2 checks. Globs may overlap only when one is provably nested and the outer group denies it. An amendment changes globs only and may not strand a pending or claimed task. Enforcement points:
- the hook: GF-OWN-2 (inside group and claimed-task globs; unowned paths and multi-link files refused), GF-FRZ-1 contracts, GF-CONF-1 guard configs, per-group drafts;
- the engine: GF-OWN-3 (completion by the task's owner, own-group files only) and GF-OWN-5 amendments;
- the audit: replays against the map in force at each event, and GF-OWN-1 checks the seal hash;
- GF-OWN-4 attribution: a command until S4.
A project is Greenfield-Senior when its record holds gf.project.initialized; an unreadable log fails closed.

No shell and the runner (18.4). A group role is denied Bash, PowerShell and Monitor (GF-RUN-1), because judging shell text never converged. It runs commands through gf_run or eccode-gf run (GF-RUN-2), which accepts either of two kinds. A plan-pinned command is matched whole against the approved plan and run through sh -c. A pinned form of eight tools uses restricted words and fixed flags, with no shell. The wrapper, run by the frozen evidence runner, works in five steps:
1. It hashes the real tree without git: content, mode, symlink targets and git directories, with objects by name and size; .eccode/ and caches are excluded.
2. It copies the tree, minus .git and .eccode/, to the system temp directory and runs the command there with git's variables scrubbed.
3. It rehashes and fails the run (exit 99) on any change outside the caller's group or in git directories.
4. It copies back only paths the caller's group owns, listing what it discards.
5. It removes the copy.
The frozen integrity and record windows apply on top.

Identity (18.3). The actor is asserted, not bound. Three controls hold it: the hook's agent_type check, role-locked MCP servers, and text-level reading of CLI commands. A spoof buys writes and reviewer-only events, but not content-addressed artifacts. Keyed attestation is proposed, not built.

Closure (18.5). There are three steps (comprehension, critique, readiness), each with its own orchestrator-recorded dispatch with input hashes. A review counts when it is valid, is on the clean closing tree, and is by a configured reviewer role that authored nothing and is not the closer. Readiness must be go, and a no-go stands. Every finding must be resolved in one of three ways:
- fixed, through a fix-verify (defect) or a paired run (documentation);
- withdrawn by the role that raised it;
- deferred by the user with a limit id (minor, or major documentation).
At least two valid mutation batteries are required. The first comes before the first review; the last is on the closing tree after the last fix, with a reason for each survivor. Accounting must be numbers or "unmeasurable". Nothing may be recorded after closure. In owner acceptance (GF-CLOSE-6), the user lists every open finding with its severity, an L-GF id and a reason. No finding may be blocking, and the scope is accepted, not closed.

Accounting (18.6). The unit is all processed tokens, from harness snapshots at slice and round boundaries. Stale figures are "unmeasurable"; only form is enforced.

Not guaranteed:
- absolute-path writes (detected, not undone);
- changes restored within a run, and writes outside the project;
- forged appended events;
- the hook off, or no agent_type sent;
- CLI commands hidden from the text check, and the sequential-roles mode;
- two instances of one role;
- which tree a paired run saw, and its command;
- battery inputs;
- whether accounting figures are true.
